title: `jsonable_encoder` type handler for `packaging.version.Version`

- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
>>> from fastapi.encoders import jsonable_encoder
>>> from packaging.version import Version
>>> jsonable_encoder(Version("1.0"))
{'_version': [0, [1, 0], None, None, None, None],
 '_key': [0, [1], {}, {}, {}, {}]}
```


### Description

# Request

Small discussion/feature request :smile: I am happy to make this change, but I was hoping to see `jsonable_encoder(Version("1.0"))` to return `"1.0"`.

In the meantime, I can use `custom_encoder=...` :muscle: Wanted to ask if this is reasonable change before creating a pull request

answer.body:
Hello @jbmoorhouse,
Thanks for submitting your proposal.
While I understand your suggestion, I personally don't like it. There are already several ways to handle custom encoding, and since Version is just a common object, I believe the correct JSON representation is the current one, not its string counterpart.
